acceptance: Pilot wave (examples, ssb, amplab, h2odb, clickbench, coffeeshop, their assigned tests and reference pages) reaches zero discretionary comments/docstrings, preserving actual runtime strings and raw SQL payloads; new and completed-scope checks plus the parity comparator pass, and the wave lands as one PR into develop.
Pilot records elapsed authoring, review and required-check cost and any false positives/consumer omissions, then adjusts checker/ownership before broad rollout.
Fresh baseline counts distinguish owned removable text, required notices/directives, upstream material, parsed fixtures and generated payloads.

Concrete wave size limit (files, deleted lines, reviewer and CI budget) is selected and recorded from pilot evidence before broad deletion; estimated counts are not delivery commitments. Pause and revise the plan if the agreed scope, cost limit or required reviews cannot be met. Existing implementation authorization is not requested again.
Soundness paths have explicit reviewer and verification requirements and are carved out of waves into their own PRs. Pilot success is not UAT, publication or production certification.

description:
The pilot is the first integration-branch wave (W1 in the delivery plan): its members are comment-cleanup-examples, -ssb, -amplab, -h2odb, -clickbench and -coffeeshop with their assigned tests and reference pages, landed as one PR into develop. This item owns no paths of its own; it closes after the pilot has landed and its measurements are recorded, and it then sets the wave size limit for every later wave. Use the checker, the parity comparator and the API-contract replacement already delivered. Apply the full strict target, preserve actually consumed example help and SQL bytes, and compare source AST plus relevant execution behavior. Target: zero discretionary explanatory comments and authored explanatory docstrings in maintained first-party code. Only proven minimum machine directives and unavoidable provenance-bound required notices remain. Useful product strings must have an actual consumer; no inert constants, unused strings, fake metadata or dynamic __doc__ replacements. Never broaden lint/type/coverage ignores, weaken assertions, or turn unknown ownership/parser coverage into an exclusion.

Measure deletion/review/CI cost and choose module-specific wave sizes before broad sweeps. Earlier inventory: 55,003 tracked Python comment tokens; about 38,700 Python docstrings (24,701 of them in tests) once tests are counted, 2,925 Python files with comments/docstrings and 292 sole-docstring bodies, before ownership classification. Refresh counts and include non-Python surfaces. Decide an explicit file/PR/review/check budget and soundness review allocation; no skipped gates or use of comment shrink as goal credit. Execution guard: creation of this TODO is planning, not approval to execute the reviewed cleanup. Obtain later implementation authorization. Use a separate linked worktree and agent-write-preflight; preserve unrelated work. Freeze nonoverlapping code/test/doc paths with the integrator before dispatch. Module work lands through integration branches with one PR into develop, as defined in the dispatch contract in docs/development/comment-cleanup-scope.md; serialize shared test-lock checks and integration, not module edits. Required native/external soundness review remains mandatory, with no auto-merge bypass. No live cloud/stress, deployment, publication, historical-result rewriting, or unapproved external-repository writes.
